newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends stronger after testing support.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends stronger after testing support.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures ended stronger, near the day's high, after a bouncy afternoon that saw London and New York crude futures testing both support and breaking initial resistance levels, traders said.

A bearish API inventory report showing a hefty build in U.S. crude stocks last week set crude futures heading lower in early New York trade, but supports held and triggered some strong short-covering interest that took both markets to the highs.
April Brent last traded 38 cents up at $19.62 a barrel, eight cents of the high. Trade was choppy with bouts of profit taking, though outweighed by short-covering, knocking the market back.

"The big build in U.S. crude stocks was sufficient to push the markets through the psychological support but the failure to breach strong supports slightly under these levels triggered a fresh round of buying," one trader said.

Traders said some active spread play pushed the April/May backwardation out to around 24 cents compared with around 10 cents in morning business. Similar play was also seen on the spot market where one U.S. trade house was a keen buyer of paper.
Gas oil futures ended firmer but off the highs. Traders said the gains were supported by stronger crude and NYMEX products.
April gas oil futures last traded $2.00 firmer at $167.25 a tonne after touching a high of $168.50 a tonne.
Analysts said that gas oil, while technically weak, was still oversold on the weekly charts and because of this they thought the market would find it hard to move lower in the next few days.
